question: When is the deadline to apply for Price College of Engineering scholarships?
answer:
The main Price College of Engineering scholarship application deadline is **February 1**, according to the [Engineering Scholarships](https://www.price.utah.edu/scholarships) page (updated October 19, 2026). The application opens December 1.

Two other dates matter:
- **December 1:** Apply to the University of Utah by this date to be automatically considered for the college's merit scholarships. No separate scholarship application is needed.
- **February 1:** Also the FAFSA deadline for need-based scholarships.

Some individual scholarships have their own deadlines, so check the listing for any scholarship you want. For questions about your specific situation, contact the college at [email] or [phone].

question: Do I need to take the GRE to apply for the chemical engineering PhD?
answer:
Yes. According to the Chemical Engineering graduate handbook (2025–2026), GRE scores are required from all applicants, regardless of background or previous degrees, and PhD applicants need a minimum score of 160 on a test taken within the past 24 months. Older scores won't be considered. The handbook also lists a 3.25 minimum undergraduate GPA for the PhD program, and scores must be sent to the U using department code 1001.

You can read the details in the [Grad Handbook 2025–2026](https://www.che.utah.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Grad-Handbook-2025-2026.pdf). Requirements can change, so confirm with the Chemical Engineering graduate program or the [University of Utah Graduate School](https://gradschool.utah.edu) before you apply. This is general information, not an admissions decision.

question: I'm transferring to the U next fall. When do I need to apply to be considered for engineering merit scholarships?
answer:
For merit scholarships, apply to the U by **December 1**. The [Engineering Scholarships](https://www.price.utah.edu/scholarships) page (updated October 19, 2026) says transfer students who apply for admission by December 1 are automatically considered for the Price College of Engineering merit scholarship, so no separate application is needed. Selected students are notified between April and July.

The PCE General Scholarships application is a separate step, due **February 1**, and the same page lists February 1 as the FAFSA deadline for need-based scholarships. The page's dates don't list a year, so confirm them for your start term with the college's engineering advisers at [email] or [phone].

question: What Duolingo English test score do I need for the materials science graduate program?
answer:
For the Materials Science & Engineering graduate program, the minimum Duolingo English Test score is **110**, according to the [MSE Admissions](https://mse.utah.edu/admissions/) page, which was updated October 19, 2026. The department says scores must be less than two years old at admission, and it doesn't make exceptions for scores below the minimum.

The MSE Graduate Handbook excerpt I found lists 105 for Duolingo. Since the admissions page is more recent, I'd go with 110, but it's worth confirming with the department before you plan around either number. The admissions page also says Duolingo scores must be sent to the University Admissions Office directly from the testing agency.

question: When are the application deadlines for the Magdiel Financial Relief Fund in mechanical engineering?
answer:
The Magdiel Student Financial Relief Fund for mechanical engineering lists two application deadlines each year: **August 6 and December 1**. The [Mechanical Engineering Financial Information page](https://www.mech.utah.edu/grads/financial-information/), updated February 2026, gives these dates. An older application page on the same site, last updated December 2025, lists August 1 and December 10, so I went with the newer page.

Applications are accepted year-round, but decisions are made the first week of class and funds are limited. The fund is for mechanical engineering students nearing completion of their degree who face a significant or unforeseen financial hardship. Because the dates conflict across pages, please confirm with the mechanical engineering office before you apply.

question: What's the minimum GPA to get into the chemical engineering PhD program?
answer:
The most recently updated source is the Chemical Engineering [Future Graduate Students](https://www.che.utah.edu/future-graduate-students/) page (updated September 24, 2026). It says applicants need a minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 for their application to be evaluated, and a GPA of 3.3 is encouraged for PhD applicants.

An older [2025–2026 Grad Handbook](https://www.che.utah.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Grad-Handbook-2025-2026.pdf) (July 2025) lists 3.25 as the minimum for the PhD program, so the requirement may have changed. Meeting a minimum doesn't guarantee admission. To confirm the current number, contact the Chemical Engineering graduate program or the college office at [email] or [phone].

question: When is the last day to withdraw from a full-semester class this fall?
answer:
I couldn't find the exact date for this fall's last day to withdraw from a full-semester class, so I don't want to guess. The Price College [Semester Guidelines](https://www.price.utah.edu/semester-guidelines) explain the rules but point to the University Academic Calendar for the actual dates. The official calendar is at [registrar.utah.edu/academic-calendars](https://registrar.utah.edu/academic-calendars), and the Office of the Registrar can confirm the date.

Keep in mind that withdrawing after the add/drop deadline puts a "W" on your transcript and you're still charged tuition. Dropping before the add/drop deadline avoids both. If you're considering withdrawing, talk with your department's academic advisor first.

question: I'm a civil engineering grad student. When is the last day to withdraw from classes this fall?
answer:
For fall 2026, the Civil & Environmental Engineering graduate handbook lists two withdrawal deadlines, depending on your class's schedule:

- **First-half classes:** Friday, September 18. This has passed.
- **Second-half classes:** Friday, November 13. This is the one to watch if your courses run the second half of the semester.

The second-half add/drop deadline is Friday, October 23, two days from now, so it's the last day to add or drop those classes without a withdrawal. The [Civil graduate handbook](https://www.civil.utah.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Graduate_Handbook_2026-2027_0819_-ADA.pdf) (updated October 13, 2026) has the full calendar. Since I can't see your schedule or registration, please confirm your dates with the Registrar or your civil graduate advisor before you act on them.

question: What's the deadline to change a fall 2026 class to CR/NC?
answer:
I couldn't confirm the fall 2026 deadline to switch a class to CR/NC. The pages I found don't give a date for that change, and the official academic calendar wasn't available to me.

Some related rules from the college and University pages:
- Core classes used to compute your Engineering GPA need letter grades, so check with your advisor before choosing CR/NC. See the [Semester Guidelines](https://www.price.utah.edu/semester-guidelines).

For the exact date, check the University Academic Calendar or ask the college office at [email] or [phone]. Current students can also ask their department's academic advisor.

question: I'm graduating in spring 2027. When do I need to apply for graduation?
answer:

question: I'm in materials science. How long do I have to drop a class without getting a W?
answer:
In Materials Science & Engineering, you can drop a class without a "W" and without permission during the **first ten calendar days of the term**, according to the [MSE Policies](https://mse.utah.edu/policies/) page. The [MSE Handbook](https://mse.utah.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/34/2025/12/MSE-Handbook-2025-Final-v2.pdf) says the same.

The college's [Semester Guidelines](https://www.price.utah.edu/semester-guidelines) describe the drop period as running up to the published add/drop deadline. Check the [Academic Calendar](https://registrar.utah.edu/academic-calendar/) for this term's exact date, since the ten-day window is counted from the first day of classes.

Before you drop, talk with your MSE academic advisor, and with a financial aid advisor, because dropping can affect your aid. If you drop below 9 credits, you may lose tuition benefits.

question: If I retake a class, which grade counts toward my GPA?
answer:
For a Price College of Engineering course you repeat on or after August 1, 2026, the **highest** grade you earned is used to compute your GPA. For repeats before that date, the most recent grade counted. Per the [Semester Guidelines](https://www.price.utah.edu/semester-guidelines), updated June 2026, W, I, and V grades also count as having taken the class, and a course taken at another school counts as one attempt, so a second attempt generally has to be at the U.

Older department pages may describe different rules. The ECE Policy Handbook (last updated 2017) says only the second attempt counts, so check with your department's academic advisor, since that handbook may be out of date. Also, if you repeat a required class and don't earn a satisfactory grade, it could affect your graduation, so confirm your plan with your advisor before you retake.

question: Where can I find the computer engineering degree requirements checklist?
answer:
The most recent Computer Engineering checklist is the [CE checklist for 2026-2027](https://www.ece.utah.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/CE-checklist_-2026-2027-.docx.pdf), posted by the Electrical & Computer Engineering department. It lists the total degree hours (120 minimum), the 40 upper-division hour minimum, and the GPA requirements.

For questions about your own plan, ask your department's academic advisors at [ECE advising](https://ece.utah.edu/advising).

question: How many times can I attempt a required course in chemical engineering?
answer:
Chemical engineering students can take a required course up to three times, but a third attempt needs approval, and after three unsuccessful attempts you're dismissed from the major.

- **Attempts 1 and 2:** No restrictions under the college's [Semester Guidelines](https://www.price.utah.edu/semester-guidelines).
- **Attempt 3:** Requires department approval through a petition. The same guidelines say a fourth attempt requires Associate Dean approval.
- **Dismissal:** The [CH EN Undergraduate Guide & Handbook](https://www.che.utah.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/CH-EN-UG-Guide-Handbook-2025-2026.pdf) (page 10) says that after three unsuccessful attempts of any required math, science or engineering course, you'll be dismissed from the major.
- **Minimum grade:** A "C" is required in required chemical engineering, math, chemistry and physics courses. "C-" doesn't count, and a grade below "C" stops you from registering for later chemical engineering courses.

Because the handbook's dismissal rule is specific to your major, talk to a chemical engineering academic advisor before you plan a repeat, especially if you're weighing a third attempt.

question: What happens if I fail an ECE course twice?
answer:
If you're an ECE student and have two unsuccessful attempts at a course, the department places you on the **ECE Monitoring List**. Any grade counts as an attempt, including a W.

You can petition for a third attempt if extenuating circumstances or a non-academic reason kept you from passing within two tries. The petition packet includes a personal statement about your struggles and a plan for success in the third attempt, plus a time audit worksheet. The [ECE 3rd Attempt Petition](https://www.ece.utah.edu/3rd-attempt-petition/) page has the full process. Approval isn't guaranteed, so talk with your ECE academic advisor before you decide on a path.

question: How many times can I repeat a course in mechanical engineering?
answer:
I couldn't find a mechanical engineering-specific repeat policy. The college-wide policy likely applies, and it appears to allow **at most two attempts** in a course. The most recent page I found, from the School of Computing (updated August 2026), says any course may be taken at most twice, and any grade, including a W, I or V, counts as an attempt. Two unsuccessful attempts can lead to probation.

The college's [Repeating Courses](https://www.price.utah.edu/repeating-courses) page (last updated June 2023) describes the rules differently, so the details may have changed. It says only the second attempt's grade counts, and that a course taken at another institution counts as one attempt. It also says courses taken at the U can't be repeated elsewhere, and that a student who takes a required class twice without a satisfactory grade may not be able to graduate.

For a third attempt in an extenuating case, the School of Computing's policy describes a petition with a formal letter to its Undergraduate Committee. I didn't find a mechanical engineering version of that process. Please confirm with the Mechanical Engineering academic advisors or the college office at [email] or [phone] before you plan a repeat.

question: What GPA puts a materials science and engineering student on academic probation?
answer:
Based on the Materials Science & Engineering policies page, the answer depends on which threshold you mean, and the page reads a little inconsistently:

- **Probation:** The page says "Students below a 3 GPA will be placed on probation."
- **Minimum to stay in the program:** A cumulative GPA of at least 2.3 is required for courses applied to the degree. Students must return to 2.3 or higher within two consecutive semesters or may be removed from the program. Its clarification adds that a student can earn a C in individual courses and still be on probation if the cumulative GPA is below 2.3.

Per the [MSE Policies](https://mse.utah.edu/policies/) page, you need a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 to avoid probation, and at least 2.3 to stay in good standing with the degree. The page doesn't explain how these two thresholds fit together, so I'd confirm with the MSE academic advisor before relying on either number. The Computer Science and Mechanical Engineering probation rules I found use a 2.5 cutoff, but those don't apply to MSE.

question: I'm a mechanical engineering major. What are the requirements for a computer science minor?
answer:
As a mechanical engineering major, you're eligible for the Computer Science minor. Here's what the 2026-27 requirement sheet lists, for 21 to 25 credits:

- **Intro programming:** CS 1400 (4 credits), or CS 1410 (4) or the accelerated CS 1420 (4)
- **CS 2420** Intro to Algorithms & Data Structures (4 credits). You need a B- or higher.
- **MATH 1210** Calculus 1 (4 credits). You need a C or higher. Engineering calculus MATH 1310 and 1320 also count.
- **Three CS courses at the 3000 level or above** (3 credits each, 9 total)

Two notes from the sheet: CS 2100 can count as one elective if you take it at the U, and you can't hold both the CS minor and the AI minor.

To declare, meet with a Kahlert School of Computing academic advisor, who can check your eligibility and fit with your mechanical engineering plan. You can reach them at [email] or through the [academic advisor info page](https://www.cs.utah.edu/undergraduate/current-students/academic-advisor-info/). The full requirement sheet is [here](https://www.cs.utah.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/CS-Minor-26-27.pdf), and the [minors page](https://www.cs.utah.edu/minors/) has the course list.
